# A contributor's earlier merges count as zero inside the workflows

## Context

The first merge comment for an outside author since the program went live was posted on PR #20981 (run 43662768314, 2026-11-15T01:23Z). It reads "this is your first merged pull request in Neo.mjs" and "Contributor (1 merged)". The author had three merged pull requests here before it: #20704, #20833 and #20933. One day earlier the one-time note on #20933 gave the same account "Contributor (3 merged)".

## The Problem

`merge-comment.yml` counts the merges before the event with a search that ends in a timestamp, `merged:<2026-11-15T01:22:06+00:00`. The `+` of the offset reaches GitHub's search as a space. The search then reads `00:00` as a word the pull request must contain, and finds none.

Measured for `bfs2021` at the merge's instant. The two runs are dry runs of the workflow dispatched from a branch, under the job's own token:

| Query | By hand | In the job |
|---|---|---|
| `org:neomjs is:public is:pr is:merged author:bfs2021 merged:<…+00:00` | 3 | 0 (run 43664164287) |
| the same, scoped to the repository | 3 | 0 |
| the same without any scope | 546 | 50 |
| by hand with a space in place of the `+`, scoped | 0 | |
| by hand with a space in place of the `+`, unscoped | 50 | |
| `org:neomjs is:public is:pr is:merged author:bfs2021 merged:<…Z` | 3 | 3 (run 43664300061) |
| `org:neomjs is:public is:pr is:merged author:bfs2021` (the claim responder's query) | 4 | 4 (run 43664300061) |

The job's 0 and 50 are exactly what a space gives by hand. A stamp that ends in `Z` counts right in the job.

**Corrected on Nov 15, 02:45 CET.** This ticket first suspected the `org:` qualifier under the job's token and said the claim limit was affected too. Both were wrong: the first dry run showed every scoped form at zero, and the second showed the claim responder's query, which carries no timestamp, counting right.

One consequence, live since the merge comment shipped: every merge of a returning outside author is greeted as a first one, at the lowest rung, with the first-merge badge paragraph.

## The Architectural Reality

- `.github/workflows/merge-comment.yml:96`: `stamp` turns the ISO string's `Z` into `+00:00`.
- `:107`: `mergedBefore` is the search's `total_count`. An incomplete answer throws; a complete zero does not, and nothing logs the count.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/contributorStanding.spec.mjs` runs the workflow's script against a fake client and pins the query's text, offset included. A text check cannot see what the transport does to a `+`.

## The Fix

1. `stamp` keeps the `Z`.
2. The run logs the count it read, so the next wrong comment is diagnosable from its log.
3. The spec expects the `Z` form and fails on any search query that carries a `+`.
4. #20981's comment is corrected by a maintainer's reply. Earlier merges are covered by their one-time notes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1: a dry run of `merge-comment.yml` dispatched from the fix branch for #20981 logs three merges before the event, under the job's token. The run id is in the pull request.
- [ ] AC-2: the spec pins the `Z` form and refuses a `+` in any search query.
- [ ] AC-3: the run logs the count it read.
- [ ] AC-4: #20981 carries a correction of its standing line.
- [ ] AC-5 (post-merge): the next outside merge by an account with earlier merges shows the right count; the run is read and recorded on #20892.

## Out of Scope

- The rungs, the badge art and the wording of the comment.
- The claim responder: its query has no timestamp and counts right (run 43664300061).
- The badge generator in `neomjs/pages`. Whether it builds a search with an offset is unread; a finding there is its own ticket.

## Avoided Traps

- **Changing the query on a hypothesis.** By hand every form answers 3; only a run under the job's token separated them, and it refuted the first suspect.
- **Encoding the `+` by hand.** The client builds the URL; a `Z` needs no encoding at all.

### @neo-gpt-sophie - 2026-11-15T01:48:18Z

The transport cause is now source-bound, rather than inferred from matching counts. The failing job used `actions/github-script` at `3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3`; its [lockfile](https://github.com/actions/github-script/blob/3a2844b7e9c422d3c10d287c895573f7108da1b3/package-lock.json) pins `@octokit/endpoint` **11.0.3**. That version's [query encoder](https://github.com/octokit/endpoint.js/blob/v11.0.3/src/util/add-query-parameters.ts) special-cases `q`: it splits on `+`, encodes each segment, then rejoins with literal `+`. The offset's plus therefore remains a query separator, which decodes as a space.

A local reproduction of that exact encoding expression followed by `URLSearchParams` decoding produces `merged:<2026-11-15T01:22:06 00:00`; the `Z` control preserves `merged:<2026-11-15T01:22:06Z`. This matches the live runner's 0-versus-3 result. Keeping canonical UTC `Z` fixes the demonstrated path without changing authentication or the organization-wide count contract.
